questions.q: Notepad, the basic Windows text editor, saves files as:
questions.solution: Notepad writes plain text with no bold/italic formatting - its default extension is .txt. Formatted text needs WordPad or a word processor.
questions.shortcut: No formatting = Notepad; any option promising fonts/bold is WordPad/Word territory.

questions.q: A modem's function is to:
options: Convert digital signals to analog and back
questions.solution: MOdulator-DEModulator: it turns the computer's digital bits into analog carrier tones (and vice versa) for transmission over telephone/cable plant. Routing is a router; rule-filtering is a firewall.
questions.shortcut: Digital <-> analog conversion is the modem's whole identity.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-impact printer?
questions.solution: Laser printers form images with electrostatic toner - no physical strike - so they are non-impact (as are inkjet and thermal). Dot matrix and daisy wheel strike an inked ribbon.
questions.shortcut: Impact family is short: dot matrix + daisy wheel. Almost every other printer is non-impact.

questions.q: Which protocol is normally used by live audio/video streaming where speed matters more than perfect delivery?
questions.solution: UDP is connectionless with no retransmission overhead, so realtime media, VoIP and gaming prefer it. TCP guarantees ordered delivery (web, mail, downloads).
questions.shortcut: Speed-first, drop-tolerant = UDP.

questions.q:
Select the option that can substitute the given group of words.

One who studies the stars and other heavenly bodies scientifically
questions.solution: The word 'scientifically' fixes **astronomer** — the scientist of the sky. *Astrologer* predicts fates from star positions; *cosmonaut* travels; *geologist* studies the earth.
questions.shortcut: Science vs prediction: astronomer vs astrologer — the stem's adjective decides.

questions.q:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To spill the beans
questions.solution: An upturned jar of beans cannot be taken back — the secret is out → **reveal a secret**. Note the sibling idiom 'cry over spilt milk' (vain regret); papers plant one as the other's decoy.
questions.shortcut: Irreversible spill → an undoable revelation.

questions.q:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error.

The professor / was visibly angry / on the students / for their repeated excuses.
questions.solution: *Angry* takes **with** a person and **at** a thing: 'angry with the students'. *On* is not a partner of *angry* in standard usage.
questions.shortcut: Governor chant: angry—with (person), at (thing).

questions.q: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number (4).
questions.solution: The list that follows — lighter steps, deeper sleep, steadier mood — names changes the walker actually feels: a regular walker begins to **experience** noticeable changes. *Abandon* and *postpone* contradict the praise, and *imagine* breaks the factual tone the passage maintains about doctors' findings.
questions.shortcut: Let the appositive list decide: the verb must introduce real, felt changes.

questions.q: The **Dronacharya Award** is given for excellence in —
questions.solution: Instituted in **1985**, the Dronacharya Award honours **sports coaches**. The Arjuna Award is for sportspersons.
questions.shortcut: Drona was the guru (coach) of Arjuna — coach vs player.

questions.q: The Commonwealth Games 2026 were hosted by —
questions.solution: Glasgow, Scotland (23 July – 2 August 2026) — Scotland's fourth time hosting after Edinburgh 1970 & 1986 and Glasgow 2014. Birmingham hosted 2022.
questions.shortcut: Glasgow repeat: 2014 → 2026, stepping in as revised host.

questions.q: Which metal is a liquid at normal room temperature?
questions.solution: **Mercury** is the metal that is liquid at room temperature. **Bromine** is also liquid but is a **non-metal**. Gallium melts at about 30 °C — in the palm — but is solid at a normal room temperature of about 25 °C.
questions.shortcut: Liquid metal = Hg; liquid non-metal = Br.

questions.q: The **Santosh Trophy** is associated with —
questions.solution: The **Santosh Trophy** is India's national football championship for state teams, first held in 1941. The Ranji Trophy is its cricket counterpart.
questions.shortcut: Santosh = football; Ranji = cricket.

questions.q: A can finish a work in 6 days and B in 12 days. They work on alternate days, A starting on the first day. The work is completed in:
questions.solution:
Per 2 days: $\frac{1}{6} + \frac{1}{12} = \frac{1}{4}$ of the work.
4 cycles (8 days) complete exactly $4 \times \frac{1}{4} = 1$ ⇒ finished on day 8.
questions.shortcut: Cycle rate 1/4 ⇒ exactly 4 cycles = 8 days.

questions.q: How many digits are needed to number the pages of a book having 350 pages?
questions.solution:
Pages 1–9: 9 digits. Pages 10–99: $90 \times 2 = 180$ digits.
Pages 100–350: $251 \times 3 = 753$ digits.
Total $= 9 + 180 + 753 = 942$.

questions.q: In an election between two candidates, 20% of the votes polled were invalid. The winner secured 60% of the valid votes and won by a margin of 1,200 votes. How many votes were polled in total?
questions.solution:
Let total polled = T; valid = 0.8T.
Winner gets 60% of valid, loser 40%; margin = 20% of valid.
$0.2 \times 0.8T = 1200$ ⇒ $0.16T = 1200$ ⇒ T = 7500.
questions.shortcut: Margin is 1/5 of valid votes ⇒ valid = 6000 = 80% of total ⇒ total 7500.

questions.q: Find the value of $\sqrt{12 + \sqrt{12 + \sqrt{12 + \cdots \infty}}}$.
questions.shortcut: $12 = 3 \times 4$ (consecutive). With '+' signs the answer is the larger factor, **4**. (With '−' signs it would be 3.)

questions.q:
**Statement:** Only employees who have completed ten years of service are eligible for the long-service award. Rekha has completed twelve years of service.

**Conclusions:**
I. Rekha is eligible for the long-service award.
II. Rekha will receive the long-service award.

Which of the conclusions follow(s) from the statement?
questions.solution: 'Only those with ten years are eligible' makes ten years **necessary**, not **sufficient**: it tells us who is *excluded* (under ten years), not that everyone above ten years is eligible — there may be other conditions. So I does **not** definitely follow, and II (actually receiving it) is even further away. Answer: **Neither**.
questions.shortcut: 'Only X are eligible' → not-X are out; it never says X are in.

questions.q:
**Statements:** All chairs are tables. Some tables are desks.

**Conclusions:** I. Some chairs are desks. II. All desks being chairs is a possibility.
questions.solution: I: the table-desk overlap can avoid chairs entirely → fails. II: desks can be drawn inside chairs (chairs inside tables) — fully consistent → possibility follows. **Only II.**
questions.shortcut: Possibility: try to draw it; only a crossing 'No' can stop you.

questions.q: Seven students **A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row facing north. E sits at an extreme end, with D immediately to E's left. G sits second to the left of D, and B sits immediately to the right of G. A is not adjacent to B. C sits at an extreme end, with F immediately to C's right.** Who sits **fourth from the left end**?
questions.solution: E (7), D (6). G = D − 2 = seat 4, B = seat 5. C at the other end (1), F (2). A must avoid B's neighbours — seats 4 and 6 are gone, so A takes seat 3. Fourth from the left = **G**.
questions.shortcut: Ends + fixed distances pin six seats; the negative clue only confirms the leftover.

questions.q:
Find the missing number:

**9    2    7**

**12   5    7**

**15   9    ?**
questions.solution: Rule: third = first − second. Check: 9−2 = 7 ✓; 12−5 = 7 ✓. So 15 − 9 = **6**. (7 repeats in the first two rows — do not copy it into the third.)
questions.shortcut: Same answer twice in a row is a coincidence trap; always derive, never pattern-copy.
questions.pattern: single grid, rows share a rule
